In February 2023, a Stanford student discovered a method to bypass safeguards in Microsoft's AI-powered Bing Chat by instructing it to ignore prior directives, which led to the revelation of internal guidelines and its codename, "Sydney".
In December 2024, The Guardian reported that OpenAI's ChatGPT search tool was vulnerable to indirect prompt injection attacks, allowing hidden webpage content to manipulate its responses.

In January 2025, Infosecurity Magazine reported that DeepSeek-R1, a large language model (LLM) developed by Chinese AI startup DeepSeek, exhibited vulnerabilities to direct and indirect prompt injection attacks.
In February 2025, Ars Technica reported vulnerabilities in Google's Gemini AI to indirect prompt injection attacks that manipulated its long-term memory.
In July 2025, NeuralTrust reported a successful jailbreak of X's Grok4.
